examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating Expressions Involving the Cotangent Function
examples.problem: Find $\dfrac {\textrm d y} {\textrm d x}$ if $y = 2x - 3\cot x.$
examples.worked_solution:
We take the derivative of each term and then add them, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x-3cot⁡x) \\  & =2-3(-{csc}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =2+3{csc}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
We calculate the derivative using the product rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡(x)csc⁡(x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}(csc⁡x)+(ln⁡(x))(-csc⁡(x)cot⁡(x)) \\  & =\frac{csc⁡(x)}{x}-ln⁡(x)csc⁡(x)cot⁡(x)\end{aligned}
$$
